speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation. To begin our assessment, are you experiencing any severe headache, neck stiffness, or sensitivity to light?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS).

Based on your history of taking haloperidol and your current presentation of fever and altered mentation without other infectious signs like a stiff neck or headache, this is highly suggestive of NMS. I will order blood tests to check for muscle breakdown (CK levels) and electrolyte imbalances to confirm this. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Creatine_Kinase, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel, Liver_Function_Tests.
